title: Crestline Enterprises - SOC 2 / ISO 27001 Posture Review
next_steps: Redwood to share SOC 2 Type II report and ISO 27001 cert via secure link
Schedule controls mapping workshop between Redwood compliance and Crestline on 2026-08-12
Customer to provide control matrix template and list of regs/data residency constraints
action_items: Sam Patel (Redwood SE): Upload SOC 2 Type II report and ISO 27001 certificate to shared trust center link (due 2026-08-07)
Ava Martinez (Redwood AE): Send pricing for Dedicated + Private deployment options and SOC add-on (due 2026-08-06)
Maya Gomez (Crestline): Share Crestline controls matrix and required evidence types (due 2026-08-11)
Jordan Liu (Redwood): Set up a 60-min controls mapping workshop and invite stakeholders (due 2026-08-06)
summary: Redwood walked through SOC 2 and ISO 27001 posture, trust center access, controls mapping process, RBAC/SSO, audit logs, encryption/KMS options, and data residency implications. Crestline requested reports and a controls mapping workshop to align evidence requirements. Next steps agreed to share reports and schedule workshop.
topics: Audit logs, retention and log forwarding
Encryption, KMS, HSM and customer-managed keys
Data residency and VPC/private deployment options
transcript:
[00:00] Maya Gomez: Okay, thanks everyone for joining. we've got CISO, IT, compliance on the call. 
[00:06] Ava Martinez: Great, thanks Maya. I'm Ava from Redwood, AE — with me is Sam our SE and Jordan on compliance. we'll run through our SOC 2 / ISO posture and then map to your controls. 
[00:18] Ethan Ross: Quick note — we're looking at both hosted and private deployments; main ask is we need evidence for SOC2 and ISO for our auditors, and data can't leave EU for some workloads. 
[00:30] Sam Patel: Yep, understood. high level, Redwood maintains SOC 2 Type II and ISO 27001 for our control plane and hosted infra, we also offer Dedicated and Private for isolating data. i'll try to flag where scope shifts. 
[00:45] Priya Nair: When you say "maintain" — do you have the actual reports we can share with our auditors or do we need an NDA first? 
[00:53] Ava Martinez: We host the reports in our trust center behind SSO and an NDA gating in some cases. typically we can provide a redacted SOC 2 Type II and the ISO 27001 certificate via secure link; full reports often require an executed NDA. 
[01:06] Maya Gomez: Ok, so first step is getting the SOC2 redacted and the ISO cert. Can you also provide a controls mapping? that's the tricky bit for us — our auditors want a mapping to Crestline's control matrix. 
[01:18] Jordan Liu: Absolutely. we run a controls mapping service — we'll map Redwood controls to your control IDs and call out where customer responsibilities lie, especially around VPC, key management, and account provisioning. 
[01:30] Ethan Ross: For KMS, we use AWS KMS CMKs and prefer customer-managed keys where possible. What options do you support? 
[01:38] Sam Patel: We support customer-managed keys in Dedicated and Private. For Hosted, we offer a hosted KMS integration and for some enterprise customers we can do a bring-your-own-key workflow with a KMS proxy; technically we've also integrated with HSM partners for higher assurance. (slight cough) 
[01:53] Priya Nair: Do you have any pen test reports or vulnerability management evidence we can include? 
[01:58] Jordan Liu: We can share our pen test summary and vulnerability program overview; again some artifacts are gated. we'll include remediation timelines and CVE tracking. 
[02:08] Ava Martinez: Quick clarification — is Crestline treating Redwood as a service provider or as part of the scope? 
[02:14] Maya Gomez: Service provider for now, but auditors might want to understand subservice providers and any inherited controls. 
[02:21] Sam Patel: Right, we'll highlight subservice providers and the controls they cover. We'll also provide a mapping that indicates which controls are in Redwood's scope versus Crestline's. 
[02:30] Liam O'Connor: About logs — we need 1 year retention and the ability to forward logs to our Splunk instance. is that supported? 
[02:38] Sam Patel: Yes, we support log forwarding via secure streaming to customer endpoints. retention on the hosted side is configurable up to X months by plan; for Dedicated/Private you control retention fully. small note — hosted default is 90 days unless you buy the extended retention add-on. 
[02:55] Ethan Ross: And what about real-time audit hooks? we need user-level traces for admin activity. 
[03:01] Jordan Liu: We capture admin API calls, role changes, token usage; those show up in audit logs with timestamps and actor IDs. for higher fidelity we can enable token-level tracing and longer retention. 
[03:12] Maya Gomez: SSO/Provisioning — we use Azure AD SCIM and want SAML SSO. what's your maturity there? 
[03:20] Sam Patel: We support SAML SSO, OIDC, and SCIM provisioning. setting up groups and role-based access is straightforward; we recommend mapping IdP groups to Redwood roles and using SCIM for automated provisioning/deprovisioning. 
[03:33] Priya Nair: How granular is RBAC? can you restrict model access per team and audit who called which model? 
[03:40] Jordan Liu: Yes, RBAC lets you define roles per route/model, and audit logs record model invocation events. there are a couple of places where naming is inconsistent — the transcript may say "KV cash" sometimes vs KV cache — but in practice our logs include model id, route, tokens used, and caller. 
[03:56] Ava Martinez: On data residency — for EU-only workloads we'd recommend either Hosted with region pinned or Private/VPC or Dedicated in EU regions. the Private deployment gives you the cleanest separation. 
[04:07] Ethan Ross: If we go Dedicated in EU, does the SOC 2/ISO scope change? 
[04:12] Jordan Liu: The reports are for Redwood's control plane and hosting environment; Dedicated/Private deployments have their own attestation notes. in many cases we provide a carve-out or a dedicated attestation note for customer-owned instances. we'll document the scope in the mapping. 
[04:26] Maya Gomez: Auditors often ask for evidence of encryption at-rest and in-transit with details on key rotation. can you provide those specifics? 
[04:35] Sam Patel: Sure — we use TLS1.2+ for in-transit, at-rest AES-256. for hosted we manage keys, but we support CMKs for Dedicated/Private and rotation policies are documented. i'll include rotation cadence and certificate management docs in the bundle. 
[04:48] Priya Nair: Is there MFA for admin console? 
[04:51] Jordan Liu: Yes, MFA is required for privileged accounts; SSO enforces your IdP MFA policy as well. 
[04:57] Liam O'Connor: Any limitations on exporting raw transcript data or PII handling? we plan to feed some support transcripts into analytics but need assurance on redaction. 
[05:06] Sam Patel: We have data classification and PII handling controls. redaction tooling is available, and in Private deployments you can disable certain telemetry. we'll call out where logs might contain PII. 
[05:18] Maya Gomez: Can you walk me through the trust center link and what we can expect to see? 
[05:24] Ava Martinez: Sure, the trust center is a secure portal — you get a link to redacted reports, scope docs, summary evidence (pen test summary, audit logs schema), and a controls matrix export. access is behind SSO and NDA for full docs. i'll send the link after the call. 
[05:39] Ethan Ross: About the controls mapping workshop — what's the typical output? 
[05:43] Jordan Liu: We produce a spreadsheet mapping Redwood controls to your control IDs, indicate evidence artifacts (e.g., report page, config screenshots, log extracts), and list control ownership. we'll also flag gaps and remediation steps. 
[05:55] Maya Gomez: That sounds good. also auditors may request on-site interviews — how do you handle that? 
[06:02] Sam Patel: We support auditor requests; we can coordinate a read-only session with our compliance team and provide time-boxed access to evidence. 
[06:10] Priya Nair: Any SLA or contractual language around breach notifications and incident response? 
[06:15] Ava Martinez: Yes, our enterprise agreements include incident notification timelines, 72-hour preliminary & ongoing updates, plus a post-incident report. specific SLAs depend on product (Hosted vs Dedicated) and contract. 
[06:27] Liam O'Connor: One more tech detail — do you persist KV caches across restarts? asking re: ability to reproduce inference results. 
[06:33] Sam Patel: The runtime keeps KV cache ephemeral for security; for deterministic reproducibility you can snapshot inputs and model versioning is supported. 
[06:41] Ethan Ross: Ok, next let's talk evidence packaging — what will you actually share after this call? 
[06:46] Ava Martinez: We'll share: (1) redacted SOC 2 Type II report pdf, (2) ISO 27001 certificate and scope statement, (3) pen test summary, (4) controls mapping template and example, (5) logging schema and retention notes, (6) KMS/key management docs, (7) trust center link and instructions. 
[07:02] Maya Gomez: Great. any notable compliance gaps we should expect? 
[07:06] Jordan Liu: Most customers find a few items around customer provisioning or data residency controls that need joint ownership. We'll call out those as "shared" controls. nothing unexpected. 
[07:16] Priya Nair: For the redacted SOC2, will it include CC6/CC7 style sections? auditors ask for specific control IDs. 
[07:23] Sam Patel: Redacted reports usually preserve control descriptions; if auditors need the mapping to your IDs we'll do that in the controls workshop. 
[07:31] Ethan Ross: Onboarding timeline — if we wanted to pilot in EU hosted, how long to get SOC docs and start a pilot? 
[07:38] Ava Martinez: We can share docs within 48 hours; pilot provisioning for hosted EU region is typically a few days once accounts are approved. Dedicated/Private takes longer — weeks depending on procurement. 
[07:50] Maya Gomez: Procurement — our procurement and legal will need vendor security addendum and DPA. do you have standard templates? 
[07:57] Ava Martinez: Yes we have DPA, SSAE/SOC addendums, and a security questionnaire. i'll route legal templates and the DPA. 
[08:06] Liam O'Connor: Regarding split-key HSM or BYOK options — any references/certifications? 
[08:12] Jordan Liu: We have integrations with FIPS 140-2/3 HSMs via partners and can provide diagrams and vendor attestations. we'll include that in the KMS docs. 
[08:21] Priya Nair: Are there any limitations for telemetry exports for EU customers? 
[08:27] Sam Patel: No functional limitations; just routing and residency rules. for hosted EU we route logs to EU regions; for Private you control endpoints. 
[08:34] Maya Gomez: Ok good. can you give an example of evidence items for, say, access control? 
[08:39] Jordan Liu: Example evidence: IdP configuration screenshot for SSO, SCIM provisioning logs, RBAC role-to-group mapping export, audit log excerpt showing user role change, and policy screenshots showing MFA enforcement. 
[08:55] Ethan Ross: If we need a custom control for regulatory variance, are you open to adding controls or process changes? 
[09:01] Ava Martinez: We do customization for enterprise customers subject to contract; we'll scope effort during the controls mapping workshop. 
[09:09] Maya Gomez: Timing to wrap up — let's confirm deliverables and dates. 
[09:14] Ava Martinez: Deliverables: SOC 2 redacted + ISO cert by 2026-08-07, controls mapping workshop scheduled for 2026-08-12, trust center link + legal templates by 2026-08-06. 
[09:28] Priya Nair: Works for me. 
[09:31] Liam O'Connor: One minor question — retention for audit logs for Hosted extended retention add-on, is that per-account billing? 
[09:37] Sam Patel: Yes, extended retention is an add-on billed per GB/month. we'll include pricing. 
[09:44] Maya Gomez: Perfect. anything else? 
[09:47] Jordan Liu: i'll also include a sample mapping file so you can pre-populate your control IDs ahead of the workshop. 
[09:54] Ava Martinez: Thanks everyone — we'll follow up via email with the links. 
[09:58] Maya Gomez: Thanks — talk soon. 
[10:01] (call ends)

Notes on transcript quality: occasional mis-transcriptions of product names (e.g., "KV cash" vs KV cache, "Redwood Dedicate" vs Dedicated) and some filler words; conversational and sales + compliance-focused.
